A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 4D-RGPT/P4D research and R4D-Bench benchmark. Their complete 23-page contents, including equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A1–A3, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, temporal-perception experiments, and qualitative results, including additional 15B-model results in Appendix A3.

after.justification: v3 retains the original evaluations and ablations in Section 6 and Appendix A3, and adds quantitative information about benchmark curation and teacher processing time.

M1.justification: The architecture, latent and explicit distillation, timestamp positional encoding, and training losses are unchanged. Naming L4P and its pretrained weights explicitly in Section 4.2 repeats the teacher configuration already specified in v1 Section 6.1 and Appendix A1.1.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same training datasets, six existing evaluation benchmarks, R4D-Bench's nine task categories, and TimeBench. The revised appendix QA count concerns sample size, with no documented change in task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main and appendix tables, including the general MLLMs, specialized spatial models, and alternative training strategies. The two newly cited distillation works are discussed as related work, not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix A2.1 changes the reported final R4D-Bench size from 1,517 to 1,419 QA pairs. However, v3 Section 5 still reports 1,517, leaving the actual evaluation size unresolved; this establishes a reported sample-size revision, not that evaluations were rerun. Other stated settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A2.1 adds a limited quantitative assessment of automatic curation quality: more than 50% of candidate samples required human correction or removal. The model ablations, TimeBench analysis, training-data analysis, and qualitative cases are otherwise unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the model evaluations. The added curation percentage does not introduce an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v3 newly reports the greater-than-50% correction/removal finding and approximately 300 ms for L4P to process 16 frames on an A100. Existing benchmark and ablation scores remain unchanged as printed; for example, Table 3 retains 42.2 for 4D-RGPT-8B and 37.9 for NVILA-Lite-8B. No new performance gain is established.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, representation equations, timestamp encoding, and loss formulations in Equations 1–7 and A8 are unchanged. No new assumptions, derivations, propositions, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: 4D-RGPT, training-only P4D distillation, and R4D-Bench. The claims of improved 4D understanding without additional inference cost and the headline performance improvements are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix A3 adds an explicit limitation concerning precise numerical estimation and attributes failures to the absence of step-by-step reasoning during training, without a new experiment testing that explanation. Appendix A2.1 also uses the newly reported correction rate to emphasize the necessity of human verification.

D1.justification: The front page adds direct GitHub and dataset access links. Appendix A1.1 newly specifies L4P's 1,337M parameters, approximate processing time and hardware, and the option to precompute its signals offline. Existing training hyperparameters, loss weights, and checkpoint specifications remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds Multimodal Distillation for Egocentric Action Recognition and Masked Video Distillation, distinguishing their distillation into vision-only encoders from the proposed approach. The remaining cited works and broader research positioning are retained.

P1.justification: Edits include renaming Section 3 to 'Preliminaries and Notations,' clarifying the teacher description, shortening the appendix training-data discussion, and revising acknowledgments and front-page text. The overall organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Existing displays are repositioned: Figure 5 moves from page 8 to page 9, Table 5 switches columns, and several appendix displays shift within the layout. Table A4's caption is shortened. No figure or table is added or removed, and the visual examples are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves documentation through direct resource links, teacher-cost information, curation-quality reporting, and explicit limitations. However, Appendix A2.1 introduces a 1,419-versus-1,517 QA-count disagreement with Section 5 while retaining the existing evaluation scores. The PDFs do not establish whether this reflects a reporting error or a changed evaluation set. These documentation benefits and the new ambiguity surrounding the central benchmark prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
